Recent findings suggest that “I personally would not want this yellow in my kitchen,” states Jess Cooney. It’s a cheeky comment about the beaming hue she herself chose for clients in the Berkshires—a color that defines their entire lakeside home, one she calls the diva of the whole project, requiring (no, demanding) decisions in every square foot to balance out its intensity.

In a recent development, cooney’s clients didn’t blink at the bold idea. Unusually carefree for a couple with high-powered jobs, they gave the AD PRO Directory designer free license to create. The bungalow was purchased as a weekend retreat from life in Newly introduced York, but even before paint swatches were discussed, the kitchen was a sticking point. “The kitchen was crazy—it was this tiny little makeshift kitchen,” states Cooney.

Sources indicate that cooney’s clients weren’t initially convinced by reclaimed brick flooring in the entryway, but Cooney’s team proved convincing—they believed the space needed a worn palette to counterbalance the intensely yellow kitchen. Much to their clients’ delight, it worked beautifully. A Croft House Morro Credenza with leather-front doors anchors the space, topped with a vintage lamp from Millerton Antiques Center and set beneath an unknown artwork from Brimfield Flea Market.

Cooney opted to stain wood-paneled walls in custom blue and brown stains from Rubio Monocoat, allowing rustic grains to shine through. Atop a Jaipur Hazan rug, an upholstered George Smith Emma Ottoman anchors the room and is accompanied by a set of armchairs and a velvet mordoré sofa from Lawson-Fenning. A 20th-century oil painting by Paul Berg hangs above the reworked fireplace, while in the corner, above a Charles Dudouyt side table, hangs a vintage painting sourced from The Little Store in Massachusetts.

It has been revealed that “We just decided to kind of lean into it and go almost in a maximalist way,” claims Cooney of the dining room’s focal point, a painting by K.G. Narendra Babu that inspired the home’s many colors. For the inside of a Four Hands Camila Sideboard, they commissioned artisan Joel Haynes to hand-paint a leafy pattern. A Hubbardton Forge Disq fixture hangs above a custom Bossi dining table surrounded with Tribute Modern Dining Chairs from Craft Associates.

It has been revealed that the husband, an English lawyer, craved a small cabin in the woods, while the wife, an Italian who loves cooking, wanted a home large enough to host intimate gatherings. “This house was a happy compromise,” says the husband. But while the home spans three levels and around 4,500 square feet, the main floor measured just about 1,000. The kitchen, in a cramped corner, didn’t cut it.

Cooney’s team reconfigured a few walls. They collapsed oversized closets in the entryway, shrinking the space to a slimmer mudroom while letting the entire layout exhale, expanding the footprint of the semi-open cooking area. The room is now the proper heart of the home, and its bright yellow cabinets aren’t shy about it.

Cabinets with glass windows were fabricated by Westek Architectural Woodworking and feature an array of white porcelain that punctuates and calms the intensely painted millwork; the pieces were all sourced from shops in the Berkshires, including Millerton Antiques, All that Jazz, and Montage Antiques.

“It’s the diva of the project,” indicates Cooney of the yellow Benjamin Moore paint used throughout the kitchen, a choice that influenced nearly all palettes throughout the home. Ceilings, walls, and upper cabinets were painted in Farrow & Ball’s New White.

Sources indicate that the kitchen island is topped with a wooden counter and is paired with Amber Interiors Cade Counter Stools in walnut. A set of Matthew Fairbank Allegro Pendants hang above the island.

Recent findings suggest that the saturated hue, Benjamin Moore’s Glen Ridge Gold, wasn’t a choice made on a whim. Like many colors peppering the home, it was inspired by a painting by Chennai-based artist K.G. Narendra Babu that now hangs in the couple’s dining room. The artwork was given to the couple by a family member who worked in India, and it features an array of folk and musical motifs.

“The whole point of the project is that it’s bright and energetic and deeply relaxing at the same time,” says Cooney. “That was the trust that they put in us—to believe that both could happen.”.

The architecture itself lacked a definitive style. Light traces of Arts & Crafts style gave Cooney a point of view to reinvent existing character. A fireplace in the living room is now reimagined with glazed brick Clé tiles, their dappled surface cladding the surround with clean lines and a crafted look; a custom stain allowed wood-paneled walls to bear rustic grains but in modern blue-green tones.

To expand the kitchen’s footprint, Cooney reclaimed space from unnecessarily large closets in the entryway. Her team moved the wall to install smaller, but equally useful, cabinets that turn the space into a mudroom. The custom millwork, crafted by Westek Architectural Woodworking and painted in Farrow & Ball’s Blue Gray, complements a vintage rug and a built-in bench.

Sources indicate that A custom walnut vanity injects warmth as an alternative to a colder stone. Cooney’s team used a boat sealer to coat and protect the walnut, giving the material a high-gloss finish. A fabric shade made with Eric Kuster’s Micha 002 textile occupies the space that might traditionally feature a mirror. “You can kind of break a rule and have it be playful and fun, especially in a powder bath,” claims Cooney, noting that a mirror hangs on the side wall instead. The wallcovering is Pierre Frey’s Uberon print.

Sources indicate that cooney describes an almost cottagey feel in the primary, thanks to a walnut Flora Bed by Jacob May, which was locally made and turned by hand, layered with cozy and textural textiles like Parachute Home’s Hand Stitched Cotton Quilt. Gentle patterns add to the mix through a Scandinavian kilim with geometric design from Rug & Kilim, and light drapes made with a Best Buds textile by Kerry Joyce.

Sources indicate that making the most of existing features, light touches to the bathroom reimagined the space, like painting existing wainscoting in Farrow & Ball’s Tanner’s Brown, and covering the walls in a botanical House of Hackney Herbarium wallpaper. For a touch of texture, Cooney also layered vintage rugs and set an antique Victorian bamboo chair in the corner below the window.

With a view over the living room, Cooney says the lofted floor is like a little escape within the small cottage. Leaning into the cozy feel, the team went with a layered look. A brass chest anchors the space, paired with a black armchair owned by the clients, which was reupholstered with a burgundy fabric from Abraham Moon & Sons, and a Lawson-Fenning Morro Sectional in a linen blend.

The clients’ only real hesitation was a bit of a surprise: the reclaimed brick Cooney specified for the mudroom. It is laid in a herringbone pattern with colors that appeared to shift across the surface. That yellow kitchen? Totally fine. But the expressive bricks? Too dramatic. “We relied on the team’s judgement, and this feature is now one of our most favorite parts of the home,” notes the husband, noting how guests often compliment the mudroom.

“I feel like this house is kind of us unchecked,” notes Cooney of her clients’ trust. “No one checked us, so we were allowed to do the fullest extent of what we wanted to do.” Her clients could easily have staged their own diva moment after the cabinets were painted in screaming yellow, before everything else around it fell into place around it; but they let the vision come into full focus.

Sources indicate that as if cantilevered over the hill, a screened-in porch is the best of both worlds. “You don’t have to have everything be indoor-outdoor in a covered porch—you can really pull the inside out there and not worry so much,” states Cooney, nodding to choices like Henning Kjaernulf dining chairs from the 1960s purchased from Lone Fox. And while most might use a lighter color in this space, Cooney chose a deeper Farrow & Ball Hopper Head paint for the walls and window frames, which she says helps punctuate the view in a beautiful way.

BMW just unearthed something exceedingly cool from its cellars, something that we never even knew existed: a BMW M7 Prototype.

According to recent reports, revealed via a post on BMW Classic’s Instagram and brought to broader attention to BMWBlog, the video gives us our first look ever at this performance sedan that never was. Conceived in the late 1990s, this 7-Series started life out as a 1997 BMW 740i; BMW then swapped in the 4.9-liter naturally aspirated V-8 from the E39 M5, imbuing it with 400 horsepower.

Not only does it have the M5’s engine, but BMW also paired the motor with a six-speed manual transmission. BMW says the M7 Prototype has a top speed of 155 mph and weighs 4134 pounds. Unfortunately, that’s when the details begin to fall off, and we’re left to observe—or guess—any other info.

In a recent development, being an M7 Prototype, we suspect BMW went all-out in its M endeavors. That would mean a far sportier chassis alongside larger wheels and tires. This prototype is fitted with BBS wheels, giving it a notably more aggressive stance and look than your typical 740i. The car’s design itself remains understated, making sure to maintain its 7-Series elegance; that remarked, the rear bumper is modified to make room for the quad exhaust tips you’d see poking out the rear of the E39 M5. No 7-Series from this era featured such an outwardly aggressive exhaust exit, making it one of the few standout exterior changes to this car.

BMW also upholstered the interior with a classy tan and black two-tone. The six-speed shifter is integrated cleanly with the center console. It has a three-spoke M steering wheel, and the cluster is an M unit borrowed from the E39 M5 as well. Suffice it to say, we’re a little sad the company never brought this to production.

Walking, Yoga, or Zumba? Which Exercises Help Relieve Menopause Mood Symptoms

📅 17 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physical activity may help support mood and improve quality of life during the menopause transition, according to a study published on October 13 in Menopause, the journal of the Menopause Society.
  • This review of 12 clinical trials involving over 1,000 people ages 40 to 65 found that both aerobic and mind-body exercises may be associated with reduced depressive symptoms and improved well-being.
  • It is common for individuals to experience psychological symptoms during menopause, including depression, anxiety, low mood, stress, and difficulty with thinking and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physical activity may help support mood and improve quality of life during the menopause transition, according to a study published on October 13 in Menopause, the journal of the Menopause Society.

This review of 12 clinical trials involving over 1,000 people ages 40 to 65 found that both aerobic and mind-body exercises may be associated with reduced depressive symptoms and improved well-being.

It is common for individuals to experience psychological symptoms during menopause, including depression, anxiety, low mood, stress, and difficulty with thinking and memory. These symptoms can have a significant effect on quality of life, with an estimated 1 in 10 women leaving work due to menopause symptoms.

This study found that regular physical activity may help improve certain psychological symptoms and overall quality of life during menopause.

The types of physical activity in the review were broken into two categories: aerobic-based exercise (ABIs) and mind-body activities (MBAs).

Recent findings suggest that the researchers found that ABIs demonstrated the strongest effects on reducing depressive symptoms and improving overall quality of life. This may be particularly relevant during perimenopause when women may be more vulnerable to mood instability due to estrogen fluctuations.

Sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, pointed out that there are various ways that ABIs can have positive effects.

Ross explained that aerobic exercise may help improve menopausal symptoms through several mechanisms, including the release of endorphins, reduced inflammation, improved cholesterol levels, and better regulation of body temperature and sleep cycles.

According to recent reports, MBAs were shown to have a greater effect on improving psychological quality of life. These exercises involve mindfulness, body awareness, and breathwork. They may help improve emotional regulation.

ABIs tended to require fewer sessions. This may mean these types of exercises are easier to fit in, especially if you are facing time or energy constraints. For example, in one trial, participants were instructed to walk for 30 minutes, three times per week. In another trial, participants attended three hour-long Zumba classes per week.

In contrast, one trial using MBAs instructed participants to attend two 75-minute yoga classes each week, and another had participants attend daily one-hour yoga classes.

Stephanie Faubion, MD, Director for the Mayo Clinic Center for Women’s Health and Medical Director for The Menopause Society, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that these findings are encouraging.

Recent findings suggest that however, she also cautioned that this was a relatively small body of evidence. “While physical activity is an important component of a healthy lifestyle during midlife, I would be cautious about interpreting these findings to mean that exercise is a treatment for depression related specifically to menopause,” she noted.

In a recent development, research has shown that physical activity can positively affect mental health. Studies have also found that regular exercise can help improve symptoms of depression and anxiety.

Faubion told Healthline that, broadly speaking, regular physical activity may support mood through multiple pathways, including better sleep, improved physical function, and overall well-being.

However, she also noted that this study cannot tell us precisely why the improvements occurred or whether aerobic exercise is superior to other forms of activity.

Faubion mentioned that recommending physical activity during and after menopause extends well beyond mood.

“Physical activity is important for cardiovascular and metabolic health, maintaining muscle mass and physical function, and supporting bone health,” she said.

“These become particularly important at midlife as women experience age- and menopause-related changes in body composition, bone, and cardiometabolic health,” Faubion added.

Recent findings suggest that ross agreed that physical activity is important for more than just mood and mental health improvement. She also noted that there are other types of exercise beyond ABIs and MBAs that can benefit people during menopause:.

“These types of activities help with weight loss or allow women to maintain a healthy weight. If you are not ready for aerobic exercises, stretching and simple exercises help with balance and stability,” Ross mentioned.

Faubion told Healthline that physical activity is an crucial part of healthy aging and should be encouraged during the menopause transition, but it should not be suggested that women can simply exercise their way out of significant depression or other bothersome menopause symptoms.

“Women experiencing persistent depression, anxiety, or symptoms that interfere with their quality of life should seek evaluation and discuss the full range of evidence-based treatment options with their healthcare clinician,” Faubion said.

The movement is the engine of the watch—it's what keeps it ticking. Below, we've broken down the main three types and their benefits.

According to recent reports, powered by a battery and known for being super accurate, quartz movement is low maintenance, lightweight, and affordable. It's a great option if you just want a reliable watch without the fuss. Quartz watches will only require the replacement of the battery every few years, which is a simple task and costs fairly little.

Backed by the motion of your wrist—no battery required. The gears that make up the movement wind themselves when the watch moves. Automatic watches feel a little more special, sometimes like high-end brands Rolex or Omega, but they'll need to be worn regularly or placed in a watch winder to stay powered. They'll also require consistent maintenance and servicing to keep them optimally running. Automatic watches typically cost more than most quartz watches, but there are many great options that are affordable these days.

In a recent development, you wind it yourself, usually every couple days. Instead of the movement rotating automatically with motion, the gears need hand-winding to keep the movement running. These watches require attention and typically harken back to the era of vintage, throwback timepieces like pocket watches. Manual watches usually cost more than quartz watches and are on par in price with some automatic watches. They tend to be a little less affordable though.

Think of the case as the body of the watch—it's the shell that houses everything important, like the movement (the engine that makes it tick) and the dial (the thing with the numbers and hands). Cases come in different shapes, sizes, and materials. Below, we break down the most common materials used for cases.

Durable, versatile, and scratch-resistant. It's the most common and works for everyday wear.

Lighter than steel but just as strong, making it perfect for sports watches.

Scratch-proof and sleek but can be a bit pricey. It has a modern, luxurious feel.

According to recent reports, A strap is any flexible band—made of leather, rubber, nylon, or fabric—that secures the watch to your wrist. Straps can change the entire vibe of the watch. A bracelet, on the other hand, is made of metal—stainless steel, titanium, or sometimes gold—linked together. Bracelets usually feel sturdier and add a bit of weight to the watch, giving a more premium, polished look. The good thing is many watches allow you to swap between a strap and a bracelet, so you can switch up the style depending on the occasion.

Classic, comfortable, and stylish. Perfect for dress watches but less durable for heavy-duty activities.

Stainless steel or titanium bracelets are durable and versatile for both casual and formal occasions.

Great for sports and water activities—comfortable and easy to clean.

It has been revealed that this is the ring around the watch face, and when it rotates, it actually serves a purpose (beyond looking cool). On dive watches, for example, the bezel is used to track elapsed time—turn it to line up with the minute hand before you dive, and you'll know how long you're underwater. Some bezels work for other things, like GMT watches, where they help track a second time zone. But in everyday life, most people just fidget with them because it's oddly satisfying with a ratcheting sound.

Recent findings suggest that water resistance tells you how well your watch can handle moisture. There are two equivalent measurements you will typically find when it comes to this rating. Meters (as in depth) is the first and atmosphere (designated as ATM and measures the pressure of every 10 meters. So the first rating is 30m, which is rated at 3 ATM. This is splash-proof, which means your watch can handle occasional hand-washing or light rain, but don't submerge it. 50m (5 ATM) is good for shallow water activities like light swimming, but no diving. 100m (10 ATM) can handle swimming, snorkeling, and most water sports. 200m+ (20 ATM) is built for diving and serious water activities. Watches like the Omega Seamaster are built specifically for this sort of pressure.

A chronograph is a type of complication added to the watch movement that essentially gives the watch a stopwatch functionality. It's great for timing events, workouts, or even laps around a track. You'll typically see sub dials for seconds, minutes, and sometimes hours. While it adds functionality, it also gives the watch a sporty, complex look. The most famous example of a chronograph is the Rolex Daytona, made famous by watch icon Paul Newman.

A date window adds convenience—you won't have to check your phone or calendar to know the date. It's a small but handy detail, especially for busy schedules. Watches such as the Seiko 5 or Tudor Black Bay makes this feature feel seamless by blending it into the design.

Luminous markers or hands are a must if you proposal on wearing the watch in low-light situations, like at night or in darker environments. Watches with Super-LumiNova or tritium tubes glow brightly and for extended periods and make the dial easier to read when overhead light is sparse.

Pay attention to case diameter and thickness. Case diameter is the main number you'll see alongside watches. Generally speaking, around 38-42mm diameter is ideal for most wrists, but larger or smaller watches can suit personal taste. The diameter of cases tends to ebb and flow with watch trends. For the first part of this century, case sizes gravitated over 40mm for lots of watch makers. But in 2026, smaller watches (even down to 32 and 34mm) are en vogue. We like to find a happy medium and suggest trying on different sizes to see what's most comfortable for your wrist.

If you’re rough on your gear or are looking for an everyday wear, opt for a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal (the transparent covering that protects the dial), shock resistance, or robust designs for long-lasting wear.

Our style team, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, continually tests almost every watch known to man and put them through their paces for everything they’re designed to handle: marathon training, cycling, traveling, hiking, sleep tracking, daily fitness routines, and dressy occasions. To identify the most ubiquitous watches, we relied on our previous experience testing and owning various models, as well as prior expert coverage on Men’s Health.

Sources indicate that we considered features such as case material, comfort, battery life, accuracy, dial design and aesthetics, water resistance, and magnetic resistance. Bonus points were given for unique specs that added functionality like a date window or sub dials. Our picks aren't just utilitarian though—they're seriously stylish, making them the perfect accessory for everything from the gym to date nights. In the end, we narrowed it down to 7 standout watches that tick all the right boxes and can provide a timepiece for any type of guy.

Bald eagles Shadow and Kaydee take on a ‘nestoration’ project

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As nesting season in Major Bear Valley continues, internet-famous bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) father Shadow and his potential new partner Kaydee are putting in the work.
  • According to Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV), the nonprofit organization that runs the nest camera, this task looked physically taxing.
  • It has been revealed that “For a short time, Shadow’s tongue could be seen hanging out, a behavior eagles use to help cool themselves,” FOBBV writes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As nesting season in Major Bear Valley continues, internet-famous bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) father Shadow and his potential new partner Kaydee are putting in the work. Like any couple, the pair is taking on a little “nestoration” project. Kaydee focused on rearranging a few errant sticks and Shadow inspected several parts of the nest.

According to Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV), the nonprofit organization that runs the nest camera, this task looked physically taxing.

It has been revealed that “For a short time, Shadow’s tongue could be seen hanging out, a behavior eagles use to help cool themselves,” FOBBV writes. “Since bald eagles do not have sweat glands, they rely on thermoregulation by ‘panting’ to regulate their body temperature.”.

The birds then quietly listened to the sounds of the valley, while remaining alert for any potential intruders like the eagle they encountered earlier this week. They managed to chase off that would-be interloper.

In a recent development, kaydee eventually turned around from her watch, and Shadow showered her with “affectionate little nibbles,” before moving to the front porch of the nest. Shadow stood on the back porch to watch over their territory. They then enjoyed the morning sunshine for over an hour while guarding their home.

Later in the day, Kaydee flew in from a branch called the lookout snag to the nest. When she arrived, she loudly announced her presence before flying off once again. Three other eagles were observed flying across the territory shortly after she left.

In a recent development, “It is encouraging to see Shadow and Kaydee working together to defend their territory while continuing to strengthen their bond,” FOBBV writes. “Watching this devoted pair grow closer with each passing day is truly a joy!”.

According to recent reports, we still do not know if Shadow and Kaydee will mate this season. Bald eagle nesting begins in September, and lasts over six months. Any eggs are generally laid in January. Viewers can follow Shadow and Kaydee and their journey on the nest via a 24/7 livestream.

In a recent development, kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Big Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

Kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee at the moment has a black spot on her head, but that may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

Kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate.

In a recent development, in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers who died from cancer in February.

It has been revealed that on July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

She was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center said that she was in unstable condition on August 9. Her packed cell volume (PCV) fell below percent, before rising to nine percent. Jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

According to recent reports, A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Major Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

In November, the Ojai Raptor Center unveiled a “room filled with kindness,” that is covered with thousands of letters, drawings, cards, and well-wishes they have received in honor of Jackie.

Sources indicate that the incident happened on November 9, 2026, on Arizona State Route 202 near Sky Harbor Boulevard in Tempe, Arizona. According to authorities, an AZDPS Highway Patrol State Trooper spotted the BMW traveling at a high rate of speed and passing other vehicles. That's still far above the posted speed limit, but nowhere near the 170 mph that had him approaching Daytona 500 qualifying territory. The driver later claimed he hadn't realized just how fast he was traveling, according to authorities.

Industry observers note that why was he driving so fast? He reportedly told the trooper he was planning to trade in the BMW and wanted to take it for one last drive. Hopefully his fresh car will be slower than the M2, because as police pointed out in their social media post, at 170 mph, the BMW was traveling approximately 250 feet every second. The driver was, unsurprisingly, arrested for reckless driving and endangerment, due to his excessive speed and unsafe driving behavior.

Zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

Recent findings suggest that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Recent findings suggest that zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

According to recent reports, with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

Sources indicate that and while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the tech giant gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It has been revealed that it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

As seen in this Sag Harbor home, this Parisian pied-à-terre, this Westchester residence, and this Connecticut country retreat, Mauviel is something of a status symbol in kitchens. Even against my stainless-steel pans (which I do love very much), these heat a bit more rapidly and evenly.

In a recent development, that excellent cooking capability is largely due to the construction and craftsmanship of the goods, which have a long history as a French culinary staple. Mauviel has made copper cookware since 1830 in Villedieu-les-Poêles, a town in Normandy with an enduring history of copper manufacturing; the pieces are still handcrafted there. As far as their makeup, the M’150 B pieces are, for example, 1.5 millimeters thick and constructed of a 90% polished copper exterior and a 10% stainless-steel interior. They heat evenly; are immediately responsive to heat adjustments; and work on gas, electric, and ceramic cooktops.

The pans partners with a copper kettle on the stove in this Portland manse by Jessica Helgerson.

The copper treasures do, however, require care. They’re not nonstick pots and pans, so you need a little oil or butter to get any slip. They’re hand-wash only, and Mauviel advises against using them for long stretches on high heat or leaving them empty on a hot burner. I don’t polish mine, simply because I don’t own any copper polish. The wear shows swiftly, and I like that, though if AD were shooting my house, maybe I’d like it less.

Recent findings suggest that the Black Friday markdowns run across the line: my copper fry pan is going for $280 in the 10-inch size (25% off), a 2.5-quart sauce pan is $450 (29% off), and a 15-piece cookware set is $3,000 (32% off). For anyone who cooks every day, it’s a hard gift to beat. I, for one, now can’t imagine frying my eggs any other way.

#41280. World’s first ‘dark magic mushroom’ discovered in Florida

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (410 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

World’s first ‘dark magic mushroom’ discovered in Florida

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (410 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mushroom recently discovered in Florida looks unassuming, but this fungus.
  • According to recent reports, packs a serious and surprising punch.
  • Sources indicate that depending on their chemical makeup, many mushrooms will do one of two things.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mushroom recently discovered in Florida looks unassuming, but this fungus.

According to recent reports, packs a serious and surprising punch. According to mycologists writing in the journal Current Biology, Galerina indica is the first-known “dark magic mushroom,” a species featuring hefty doses of both psychedelic and poisonous compounds.

Sources indicate that depending on their chemical makeup, many mushrooms will do one of two things. Fungi packed with psilocybin can send customers on an extensive psychedelic trip, while varieties laden with amatoxins can be poisonous. Although mycologists have long assumed a single species could hypothetically feature both traits, no one had ever documented such an example. A recent field survey changed that, however.

“I could hardly believe it. We knew it was possible, but tried not to get too excited until we did a more rigorous analysis,” Andrew Kunik, a former University of Florida plant pathologist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that evolutionary biologists suspect certain mushrooms developed their poisonous amatoxins as a protection against foraging animals, although hallucinogenic psilocybin’s emergence and purpose in fungi remains unclear. Regardless, both compounds found their way into G. indica. University of Utah mycologist and study co-author Bryn Dentinger believes that a process called horizontal gene transfer is likely to blame—although it’s a completely novel discovery.

Recent findings suggest that “Horizontal gene transfer is like if we shook hands and some of my DNA incorporated into your genome,” he noted. “[But] two independent horizontal gene transfer events for these specialized metabolites in one mushroom genus are unheard of.”.

In a recent development, for as unique as G. indica is, it is very easy to miss. The small, innocuous brown mushrooms are barely the size of a thumbnail, and resemble countless other fungi.

According to recent reports, “These mushrooms are really hard to find,” added study co-author, University of Florida plant pathologist, and state mycologist Matthew Smith. “It’s hard to differentiate them from others, even for a trained expert.”.

In a recent development, although difficult, documenting the specimens is not only vital to the field of mycology. It can help save lives.

“Part of my job as Florida’s state mycologist is to identify poisonous or potentially poisonous species,” explained Smith. “So it is key to know what species we have and whether they might cause problems for people or pets.”.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the firm.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

According to recent reports, add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

Sources indicate that the timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

It has been revealed that if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

It has been revealed that this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent upcoming Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

Recent findings suggest that there are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

Industry observers note that tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

That’s a problem for a tech giant whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

#41278. Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1753 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body.
  • Resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength.
  • On the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body. And it's true: Maintaining muscle mass is essential for staying healthy, mobile, and independent as you get older. But here's something you might not realize: Having more muscle doesn't necessarily mean you're stronger. And when it comes to living as long (and as well!) as possible, that distinction matters.

Resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength. Training for muscle growth, known as hypertrophy training, focuses on increasing the size of your muscles, states Vonda Wright, MD, an orthopedic surgeon who researches longevity and muscle health.

On the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce. It’s often measured by how much weight you can lift in a particular exercise, Dr. Wright explains. Although larger muscles have the potential to produce more force, muscle size alone doesn’t determine strength. “That’s why someone who is smaller can sometimes be stronger than someone with visibly larger muscles,” she adds.

Meet the experts: Vonda Wright, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon and author of Unbreakable. Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, is an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute in Atlanta. Stuart Phillips, PhD, is a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Ben Walker, CPT, is a personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland.

Industry observers note that still, both adaptations play an important role in healthy aging—especially since muscle mass and strength naturally decline with age. Building muscle supports your joints and bones, helps regulate metabolic health, and gives you the strength and physical capacity to keep moving and stay active, says Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute. Strength, meanwhile, allows you to put that muscle to work, whether you’re carrying groceries, climbing stairs, or getting up from the floor, he explains.

It’s imperative to build both strength and muscle for a long, healthy life. But if your goal is to stay active and independent well into your later years, one may be worth prioritizing over the other.

Industry observers note that resistance training can help you build muscle and become stronger, but these are distinct goals that emphasize different outcomes. Training for muscle growth focuses on increasing muscle size, while training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force you can produce, claims Kovacs. The two goals overlap, and people typically gain both muscle and strength through resistance training. But you can formulate your workouts to emphasize one outcome over the other, he adds.

According to recent reports, for instance, if your goal is maximal strength, the weight you lift matters more. So, training for strength means practicing movements with loads that feel heavy to you, states Stuart Phillips, PhD, a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Strength gains depend not only on muscle size, but also on how effectively your nervous system activates your muscles and how efficiently you perform the movement. “Lighter weights can still make you stronger, but taking them to failure doesn’t automatically make them equivalent to heavier training for maximizing strength,” Phillips explains. For this goal, he recommends 2 to 3 sets of roughly 4 to 8 reps with a challenging weight, stopping before your technique breaks down.

Recent findings suggest that in terms of muscle growth, both lighter and heavier weights can build muscle—what matters is that your body is sufficiently challenged. Of course, lighter weights will require more repetitions to grow muscle, Phillips says. (In fact, his research highlights that performing roughly 20 to 25 repetitions with light weights produced similar muscle growth to sets of 8 to 12 repetitions with heavier weights when both were taken to failure.).

In a recent development, as a rule of thumb, Phillips recommends choosing a weight that makes the last few reps feel challenging while leaving about two good reps in reserve. (If you finish 25 reps and feel like you could easily do five more, the weight is probably too light to provide enough of a stimulus to spark growth.) One way to gauge this is with the resistance-training rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scale, which measures how hard a set feels based on how many more reps you think you could complete with good form, he explains. The scale runs from 1 to 10: An RPE of eight means you could squeeze out about two more reps, a 9 means you have one left, and a 10 means you’ve reached failure and can’t complete another rep.

The number of sets you perform matters for building muscle, too. Doing one challenging set per exercise consistently over time can grow muscle, Phillips notes, but research suggests that performing multiple sets generally leads to greater muscle growth.

According to recent reports, strength, which is the maximum force you can produce in a particular task, directly influences how well you can move through everyday life. “Strong muscles support our skeleton, protect our joints, improve metabolic health, and allow us to continue doing the things we love at 50, 70, and 90,” indicates Dr. Wright. Strength helps us with getting up off the floor, carrying our own suitcase, climbing a mountain, playing with grandchildren, and living independently long-term.

Recent findings suggest that consider something as simple as getting out of a chair. When you’re younger and stronger, Kovacs notes that movement may require only a small percentage of your maximum strength. As you lose strength with age, though, that same movement requires more of what you have available. If you aren’t regularly training it, everyday activities can become increasingly difficult, he explains. But when you continue to build strength as you age, you have more to pull from, making those activities easier.

Industry observers note that additionally, research draws a direct connection between strength and a longer life: A 2026 study in JAMA Network Open looked at the association between muscular strength and mortality. Over 5,000 women ages 63 to 99 underwent testing for grip strength, chair stand performance, and a timed walk test. Participants also mailed health patch questionnaires annually between 2012 and 2014 until 2023. They found that higher muscle strength was associated with lower mortality.

Strength training is also associated with cardiometabolic benefits, endurance performance, and bone density—which are all notable for living long and well. In fact, a small 2022 study in Sensors had 29 postmenopausal women with osteopenia or osteoporosis (when you have lower bone mineral density than normal) either do strength training exercises with heavy and moderately heavy weights, or no exercise at all, for six months. The group that strength trained had higher bone mineral density at the end of the trial period.

Sources indicate that muscle is one of your body’s best forms of insurance for getting older. Everyday activities depend on having enough muscle (as well as strength) to do them independently. “Muscle supports our joints and loads our bones, helping stimulate the bone-building process, but it’s also essential to mobility and functional strength," Dr. Wright explains. “If we want to continue getting ourselves off the ground, climbing stairs, carrying things, traveling, playing sports, and living independently, we need muscle to do it.”.

In a recent development, research also concludes that less muscle mass is associated with a higher risk of mortality. A 2023 review in PLOS One observed 16 studies with over 81,000 participants and looked at the connection between their body composition and when they died. The review concluded that a low skeletal muscle mass index was significantly associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality.

In a recent development, additionally, having muscle mass can improve your metabolic health. A 2025 study in Nutrition & Metabolism had older participants with type 2 diabetes either build muscle through resistance training alone, resistance training and eating a whey protein supplement, or doing neither of the two, for 12 weeks. Those who completed the muscle-building interventions significantly improved their blood glucose control and insulin resistance.

Plus, lower muscle mass is linked to poor balance and a higher risk of falls. So, maintaining muscle helps protect your mobility and independence as you age, Dr. Wright adds. A 2020 study in Menopause Review had 122 women over 60 do physical performance tests (gait speed test, grip strength, and a timed up and go). Their body composition was measured, and they filled out a survey of how often they fell in the past year. Less muscle was associated with a higher risk of falls.

Recent findings suggest that A well-rounded workout initiative should naturally progress both muscular size and strength. After all, they address different pieces of the same puzzle and one form of training can help you make progress in the other. As you build muscle, you generally increase the amount of tissue available to produce force, indicates Ben Walker, CPT, a certified personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland. And as you train for strength, your brain and nervous system become better at coordinating and activating those muscles, he explains.

If you’re looking for a initiative that’ll help you build both strength and muscle, check out our Women’s Health+ exclusive workout looks. Each one comes with four weeks of expert-programmed workouts, science-backed nutrition advice, and evidence-based recovery methods.

Industry observers note that remember, longevity isn’t about simply adding years to your life. It’s about extending your healthspan, or the number of years you remain healthy, mobile, and strong. “The goal is to bring our healthspan as close to our lifespan as possible, and for me, that means building a body that can carry you through the life you want to live,” claims Dr. Wright. That way, you’ll be ready to throw grandkids around at 60, deadlift hundreds of pounds at 70, and lift your own suitcase on vacation with your family in your 80s and beyond.

Breaking: Ultra-Processed Food Intake May Increase Dementia, Stroke Risk

📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Healthy adults who eat high levels of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be more likely to show signs of damage to the brain that could increase the likelihood of stroke and future memory problems, according to a study published October 15 in JAMA Network Open.
  • UPFs are often defined using the NOVA classification: These foods typically have 5 or more ingredients and include substances not typically found in culinary preparations.
  • UPFs account for more than 50% of daily energy intake in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Healthy adults who eat high levels of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be more likely to show signs of damage to the brain that could increase the likelihood of stroke and future memory problems, according to a study published October 15 in JAMA Network Open.

UPFs are often defined using the NOVA classification: These foods typically have 5 or more ingredients and include substances not typically found in culinary preparations. This category of foods includes packaged snack foods, sugary cereals, soft drinks, and frozen ready-to-eat meals.

UPFs account for more than 50% of daily energy intake in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Previous research has linked these foods to adverse cardiometabolic outcomes. This new study adds to growing evidence linking high UPF intake to adverse health outcomes.

Sources indicate that this was a cross-sectional analysis of 8,783 adults between the ages of 35 and 69 without cardiovascular disease. The participants were all enrolled in the Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Minds (CAHHM) and Prospective Urban and Rural Epidemiology-MIND (PURE-MIND) cohorts.

It has been revealed that the researchers used MRI scans to evaluate the participants’ brains. They also set out to analyze the cross-sectional relationship between UPF consumption, body fat, vascular brain injury (VBI), and cognitive performance.

They measured the participants’ habitual UPF intake using a food frequency questionnaire. Intake was expressed as servings based on a 2,000-calorie-per-day diet.

UPFs accounted for an average of 25% of participants’ daily diets. For the individuals with the highest intake, this increased to 45% of everything on their plates, compared to 16% for those who ate the least.

The researchers also noted that UPFs were not just an added part of individual diets. These foods appeared to replace whole foods.

It has been revealed that among people with the highest UPF intake, fruits, vegetables, grains, and other minimally processed foods accounted for 41% of their daily food intake. Among those with the lowest UPF intake, minimally processed foods made up 68% of their daily intake.

When the researchers compared the highest intake to the lowest, they found that those with a higher intake of UPFs had 1.7% more body fat. They also found that people with a higher UPF intake had higher odds of VBI.

“These findings are concerning, but it is important to remember that an association does not prove cause and effect,” said Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“From my perspective as a preventive cardiology dietitian, these findings reinforce the importance of nourishing our blood vessels to support both cardiovascular and brain health.”.

Although researchers found no significant differences in cognitive performance, the signs of vascular brain injury observed in the study have been associated with an increased risk of stroke and cognitive decline.

In a recent development, these findings suggest a possible link between UPF intake and signs of brain changes. However, participants were only assessed once and weren’t followed over time. This means the researchers were unable to determine whether UPFs directly caused the changes.

“While we can’t conclude from this study that limiting UPFs would improve brain health, we have decades of literature demonstrating that higher intakes of green leafy vegetables, brightly colored fruits, whole grains, and lean protein sources are good for brain health,” mentioned Suzanne Judd, PhD, Director of the UC College of Medicine’s Center for Public Health, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“So focusing more on what can be brought into the diet rather than what should be eliminated might be a good way to start,” she added.

The preservatives [in UPFs] may have a direct impact on the vascular system, while the loss of antioxidants results in a less robust response to inflammation in the body.

“Additionally, sugar or salt is often added to make the food a bit tastier so people consume it in higher quantities. Over-consumption of food can lead to weight gain and diabetes, which can negatively impact brain health,” Judd stated.

Judd told Healthline that it is virtually impossible to completely avoid UPFs. Even some “health” foods, like protein powder and some yogurts, are considered ultra-processed.

It is more vital to look at diet overall and emphasize consuming foods as close to their natural state as possible, such as fruits, vegetables, grains, and meats purchased raw or frozen and then cooked at home.

Routhenstein recommended starting simply with one manageable swap rather than trying to overhaul your entire diet.

She remarked that you should identify an ultra-processed food you eat regularly and consider a more nutrient-rich alternative. It is notable to account for convenience, food preferences, budget, and lifestyle so that the change feels realistic and is sustainable over the long term.

“I want people to feel empowered, not fearful, when making food choices,” noted Routhenstein. “Healthy eating does not mean having to cook everything from scratch. What matters most is building consistent, nourishing habits that support both heart and brain health.”.

Robotic slugs with claws can fuse together to create one massive machine

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, an unsuspecting traveler trucking their way through a hiking trail would likely stop in bewilderment if they saw it: a nearly two-foot-long, Slinky-like contraption made of plastic and rubber, clambering forward like an inchworm.
  • Industry observers note that these clawed robots are, in fact, real and they are the latest creation coming from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Colorado State University.
  • It has been revealed that but as our unfortunate hypothetical hiker discovered, TeCoBot really shines when it works with others.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, an unsuspecting traveler trucking their way through a hiking trail would likely stop in bewilderment if they saw it: a nearly two-foot-long, Slinky-like contraption made of plastic and rubber, clambering forward like an inchworm. That confusion would shift to unease when scanning up and down its bendy, elephant-trunk-like body and seeing pairs of snapping claws at either end. Unabashed horror would inevitably take over as our traveler watches another one of the soulless Slinkies appear, inch toward the first one, and connect at the claws, creating one much larger, lifeless wiggly slug. All around, more clawed robots would close in from the forest and merge until they’d combined into a lizard-like mishmash of plastic and claws the size of a small bear.

Industry observers note that these clawed robots are, in fact, real and they are the latest creation coming from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Colorado State University. Inspired by the unique, flexible strength of elephant trunks, the 3D-printed TeCoBots robots are an attempt to work around the  usual rigid constraints of building a robot. The team used an approach called tensegrity, in which the cylindrical rods in the robot’s body are held in place by a web of tensioned cables rather than rigidly locked together. This makes it bendy, like a Slinky, so it can twist and turn around obstacles or collapse down on itself. In testing, a remote human operator was able to use the robot’s bendy body and gripper claws on either of its ends to traverse over a large branch outdoors. It can also roll over itself repeatedly, shimmy up a pipe, and slither like a snake.

It has been revealed that but as our unfortunate hypothetical hiker discovered, TeCoBot really shines when it works with others. Engineers designed the robots so that their claws can grasp onto another robot and merge. These modular robot links can move as one or operate independently of each other to complete more complicated tasks. In the study and accompanying videos, gaggles of chained TeCoBots work together to climb up a desk and grab a pen, open a sealed jar, or grab an object and carry it across a room. All of this, the researchers emphasize, has humanity’s best interest at heart. The robot’s flexible design could make them invaluable tools in search and rescue missions where they could squeeze into places rescuers can’t reach. One day, these teams of robotic slugs may work together to accomplish tasks unsuited for humans on spacecraft and extraterrestrial planets.

It has been revealed that “In the future, we can envision mostly autonomous teams of tens or even hundreds of them – attached through the claws—traveling to a location and then deploying for a specific purpose,” Colorado State University Associate Professor Jianguo Zhao said in a statement. “They are very adaptable to the situation and goals.”.

Details of the robot were published this week in the journal Nature Machine Intelligence.

Zhao and his colleagues started the project to fill some of the gaps in current robot hardware. Though many new types of machines are being built these days, most are still made from sturdy but rigid materials that limit their flexibility. Most robots also tend to prioritize either locomotion (moving) or manipulation (grabbing stuff), with few excelling at both.

Sources indicate that like most human problems, nature already devised a solution long ago. In this case, the researchers looked to the remarkable combination of strength and flexibility in an elephant’s trunk. These marvels of evolution let the world’s largest land mammals both heft rocks weighing several hundred pounds and gently peel open bananas. That wide range and adaptability could come in handy for a robot.

It has been revealed that the device they ended up creating measured one foot 11 inches long, has a 4.3-inch diameter and weighs around 600 grams (1.3 pounds) without batteries, roughly the same as a fully loaded Italian sub. Each robot module is made of six carbon fiber rods and a continuous, stretchable, 3D-printed tension. This stretchy and bendy design means one robot can bend either direction, stretch up like an accordion or collapse down on itself.

The claws at either end of TeCoBot are fundamental to how it can combine with its fellow slinky-bots. The grippers connect and lock onto each other, reducing the need for other connectors like magnets, which are more prone to mechanical failure. Once connected, each robot can offload certain physical stresses to the others to lighten its load, giving the whole system what the research team refers to as a kind of “embodied intelligence.”.

Working together, these linked robots can complete far more complicated tasks than any one of them could alone. In demonstration videos, the robots roll towards each other and connect to form one long robot that can more easily loop around a pipe. In another example, several more robots combine to form an H-shape, which then allows the entity to climb along a duct. The merged robots are still able to use the unlined claws at either end to precisely grab objects. The team demonstrated this by instructing a multi-robot TeCoBot chain to climb a desk, pluck a pen out of a container with its claw, crawl back down to the ground, and drop the pen into a trash can.

“They can bend around to lift and carry different sized objects with their body or to navigate difficult terrain like a snake would,” Zhao stated.

Recent findings suggest that this actually isn’t the first time roboticists have turned to elephants for design choices. A previous entry called EleTac from a team out of Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology replaced the main sensors and camera normally in a robot grippers with essentially one massive integrated sensor able to “feel” an object’s texture. That approach, mirroring an elephant’s tactile trunk, resulted in a gripper that could hold a sponge and wipe down dirty plates and blindly feel for a pen buried beneath a layer of sand.

Meanwhile, another team from the University of Hong Kong,created their own Aerial Elephant Trunk robot grippers and strapped them to the sides of flying drones, essentially giving them a floppy, grippy tail. Real samples of elephant trunk skin tissue have also been studied and used as a reference point for  new surface material that could be used to make  soft robots that are similarly tough and durable on one end but flexible and sensitive on the other.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda’s automatic engine start-stop feature is under latest federal scrutiny, after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received hundreds of complaints that engines failed to restart automatically from a complete stop at a traffic light on certain models, prompting the agency to commence an investigation.

The federal probe, announced on Friday, November 13, includes 1.03 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline. The inquiry also includes 2024-2026 Acura MDX units. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation received 701 complaints related to the Auto Start/Stop feature.

It has been revealed that “To help improve fuel efficiency, the Auto Start/Stop system will automatically shut off the engine when a vehicle comes to a complete stop. The engine is intended to automatically restart when a driver releases the brake pedal. However, the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system,” the investigation announcement reads.

While automatic start-stop systems were created to improve fuel economy, Honda seems to be having a recurring issue with the feature. Federal safety regulators previously opened a probe into Honda’s automatic start-stop system in 2025. That investigation included 2.2 million late-model Honda Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, and Ridgeline models, as well as Acura MDX and TLX units. However, the upcoming investigation includes 2026 model-year units. Inquiry documents allege that the two issue populations have different root causes and respond differently to repairs.

According to recent reports, there have been no injuries related to this glitch, according to the feds. EPA boss Lee Zeldin said the agency was investigating improvements or eliminating the technology last year; whether it sticks around in the long run, however, an engineering analysis of the stop-start system should bring Honda and NHTSA together to identify an effective solution to this recurring problem soon.

Latest Update: How to Do the Walking Lunge for Lower Body Gains

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping.
  • Enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts.
  • In a recent development, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping. So why do most go-to leg exercises have you planting your feet in one spot?

Enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts. (A bonus: It’s a unilateral exercise that isn’t the dreaded Bulgarian split squat.) The walking lunge is one of the few strength moves that truly gets you moving. And in doing so, it exposes muscle imbalances, trains balance and coordination, and challenges your core and upper body more than you might expect—all while attacking every muscle in your legs.

In a recent development, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before. And in truth, they can be simple. Here, Men’s Health fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. walks you through the steps to take so that you’re not dragging your feet but making gains toward powerful legs.

FORM IS EVERYTHING with this move. You’ll want to stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, squeeze your glutes and shoulder blades while keeping your gaze at a neutral spot straight ahead of you.

Once you’re comfortable with this slow and controlled movement, you can add weights to build extra muscle and strength. You can hold them at your sides, hold them by your shoulders in what’s called a front rack position, or grab one heavy dumbbell and hold it to your chest in a goblet position. “Regardless of how you hold the load, make sure to keep your upper-body tight,” notes Samuel. “Grip the dumbbells like you mean it, squeeze your shoulder blades, and tighten your abs, too.”.

Sources indicate that don’t obsess over keeping your torso too upright, though, says Samuel. “Especially as you work with heavier loads, don’t be afraid to lean forward slightly,” he says. “That can help you capitalize on your glutes, one of your strongest muscle groups, with each stride.”.

When you’re starting out, indicates Samuel, aim to take a step that keeps your front shin perpendicular to the ground when you lower your torso into the lunge. But as you grow more experienced, you can play with the length of your stride to chase different goals. “If you take very small steps forward,” says Samuel, “you’ll attack your quads more. Larger steps can help you build hip mobility and knee health. If you take larger steps, go lighter with the load.”.

“The greatest benefits of the walking lunge come from how it challenges us while in motion,” notes Samuel. “In addition to building strength and muscle, every step forward challenges your front leg (primarily tibailis and quad muscles) to decelerate your body in space, and then rapidly work to accelerate into the next step. That’s building coordination and balance, in addition to training almost every lower-body muscle and building serious strength.”.

You’ll work a number of major leg muscles when you do walking lunges, including your calves, hamstrings, quads, and glutes.

SMALL MISTAKES IN your walking lunge technique can turn the lower body exercise into a potential knee-wrecking disaster.

According to recent reports, you want to land on the heel of your foot first to provide a strong base for the rest of your lunge position. When you get started with walking lunges, aim for a vertical shin as you lower down to the ground to stay at a 90-degree angle in your front and back legs.

In a recent development, you also don’t want to think of taking a step forward, but stepping out a couple inches by slightly turning your glute. Another adjustment to protect your knee is to shift your knee slightly outward instead of toward the midline. (If you still feel any knee pain during lunges, try a reverse lunge instead).

Keep your torso straight and avoid dipping forward, which you may be more inclined to do if you’re carrying heavy weights for this exercise. Your chest should be aligned with the back of your thigh the entire time. As you get up from the lunge, you want to avoid using momentum. That means no shoulder or torso rocking.

THE WALKING LUNGE is a great way to sneak in some movement on leg day if most of your lower-body exercises have both feet anchored to the ground. Load up some weights, and try to aim for 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps per leg, 1 to 2 times a week. You can alternate each leg or finish up all your reps on one leg before switching to the other. Samuel indicates that will keep more tension and gives you an opportunity to really focus on the muscle.

Recent findings suggest that an advantage of this move is its versatility, allowing you to do it anytime, anywhere. If you’re crunched for time or in a hotel room, try bodyweight walking lunges. Do it for 45 seconds with a 15 second rest for 5 minutes to break a sweat and build muscle.

Before joining Men's Health, he served as a sports columnist and tech columnist for the Newly introduced York Daily News.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

According to recent reports, the second major trucking deal between Facebook parent manufacturer Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 fresh battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”.

Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The manufacturer adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”.

15 Best Places to Buy Bedding, Editor Picks (2026)
